criteria: Correctly explains what compression does (reduces file size)
Gives at least one concrete reason why reducing file size matters

width.minimum: Explain what data compression is and give at least one reason why it is useful (e.g. file size, transmission speed, storage cost).
width.typical: Explain why compression is important in contexts including storage, transmission speed, energy use, and bandwidth cost; compare file sizes before and after a simple compression example.
wider: Investigate the energy cost of transmitting large uncompressed files compared to compressed equivalents — connect this to environmental impact of digital systems
Examine why compression is particularly important in low-bandwidth contexts such as remote First Nations communities and what trade-offs arise

nodes.label: Lossless compression — run-length encoding
nodes.checkpoint: Students can use run-length encoding to represent patterns in data in a compressed form and explain how the algorithm works.
criteria: Correctly applies RLE to encode a simple sequence
Explains how the encoded form represents the original data
nodes.hinge_reason: RLE procedural errors cascade into N3 — students who cannot correctly encode a sequence cannot calculate compression ratios or reason about when RLE is effective versus ineffective, which is the foundation for lossy/lossless comparison.

width.minimum: Apply run-length encoding to a simple sequence (e.g. a row of pixels) and explain how it reduces storage by representing repeated values as a count-value pair.
width.typical: Apply run-length encoding to image row data; calculate the compression ratio achieved; explain when RLE is effective (many repeated values) and when it is not (random/varied data).
wider: Investigate additional lossless compression techniques (e.g. Huffman coding concepts) and explain how they generalise the principle of representing frequent patterns efficiently
Apply RLE to different data sequences and identify what properties make data more or less compressible with this technique

modes.reason: Run-length encoding requires students to apply a precise algorithmic procedure. Errors in counting runs or encoding the count-value pair are common. Sufficient practice with varied sequences — images, text repetitions, binary strings — builds the procedural fluency needed before the conceptual explanation is solid.

nodes.label: Lossy vs lossless — trade-offs and consequences
nodes.checkpoint: Students can explain the difference between lossy and lossless compression, identify contexts where each is appropriate, and describe the consequences of using each.
criteria: Correctly distinguishes lossless (exact recovery) from lossy (permanent data loss) compression
Identifies an appropriate context for each type and justifies the choice
Names at least one consequence of using lossy compression in an inappropriate context

width.minimum: Explain the difference between lossy and lossless compression and give one example of each; identify one consequence of using lossy compression.
width.typical: Explain that lossless compression preserves all original data (decompression recovers the original exactly) while lossy compression permanently discards information; describe appropriate contexts for each (e.g. medical images require lossless; music streaming tolerates lossy); explain why the same file format may not suit both contexts.
wider: Compare audiovisual codecs (MP3 vs WAV, MP4 vs uncompressed video) and explain what information is discarded and why human perception makes this acceptable in most contexts
Investigate the consequences of lossy compression in high-stakes domains — medical imaging, legal evidence, archival records — and explain why lossless is required
Explore how image compression artefacts arise (e.g. JPEG block artefacts) and explain the algorithmic reason they appear

modes.reason: The lossy/lossless distinction is abstract without concrete cases. Students need examples where the trade-off is consequential — medical imaging, audio quality, image artefacts — to understand why the distinction matters beyond a vocabulary definition.
